title: RFEM import
description: data/rfem/<model>.json, schema 1.0 -- one RFEM table export read into Woodcore (docs/open-questions.md §14). Generated by calc/rfem_import/json_export.py, never hand-edited. It is the one intermediate format between RFEM and Woodcore, and the contract its two producers meet at: RFEM's own table export, which every user has and which needs no API key, and a script driving the gRPC API, which only a Dlubal key holder has. Its four parts answer for themselves and nothing in one is derived from another at read time: `model` is what RFEM's own tables said, `metadata` is what the engineer wrote in the objects' comments, `structures` is the grouping this import worked out, and `results` is what the solver produced. Every number is in the units this project computes in -- a length in metres, a section's b and h in millimetres, a force in kN, a moment in kNm -- converted on the way in from whatever the model's «Unités et décimales» were set to, so a reader needs no unit table.

schema_version.description: -- pinned: a record written at another version is refused rather than read as this one.

source.description: Where this came from: the export's path as the project names it, what produced it, and when it was read. No key is required, so an import made by hand from a folder of CSVs is as valid a record as one a script wrote.

path.description: -- the export, as the project file names it: relative to the project's folder where it lies inside it.

format.description: -- which of the two formats RFEM's export dialog wrote.

producer.description: -- «gui» for the table export dialog, «api» for a script driving the gRPC API.

language.description: -- the language RFEM's own words are in, where it is known: the headers are localised and the load case's id with them (CC, LF, LC).

read.description: -- when the import read it, ISO 8601. The one date here: data/project.json deliberately carries none, so that an unchanged export stays unchanged to the byte (docs/conventions/build-and-release.md §12), and this file says when rather than pretending it is timeless.

rfem.description: -- RFEM's own version, where the producer knows it.

model.description: What RFEM's own tables said, as read. ⚠️ A member names its line and its section rather than carrying them, and a structure names its members rather than carrying them: one fact, one place (docs/architecture/principles.md §2 rule 1).

z.description: -- metres, positive downwards: the frame this project's figures are drawn in (docs/domain/static-models.md §3.3octies).

lines.description: -- the line number as a string against the node numbers it joins. The chain a member reaches its geometry by: member -> line -> nodes.

nodes.description: -- the nodes its line joins, resolved on the way in; empty where the line is gone, which the import reports.

type.description: -- RFEM's own word, localised: «Poutre», «Träger», «Beam». Carried and never interpreted.

b.description: -- millimetres, which is what a detail schema is drawn in (docs/domain/detail-schemas.md §3.3decies).

members.description: -- the members RFEM's own table assigns it to; its ranges («8-10») expanded on the way in.

id.description: -- RFEM's own localised abbreviation: «CC1» in French, «LF1» in German, «LC1» in English. An opaque label, never interpreted.

category.description: -- RFEM's own word for the action's category.

action.description: -- that category read into SIA 260's terms, which is what a load combination picks its factors by (docs/domain/calculation-domains.md §3.3); null where the category is one this reader does not classify.

name.description: -- as RFEM writes it: «1.35 * CC1 + 1.50 * CC2».

kind.description: -- «member_load», «nodal_load», and whatever kind of load sheet a reader introduced.

case.description: -- the load case's id. It exists because RFEM writes one load sheet per case; the gRPC object listing carries no such link.

unit.description: -- as the column's header declared it: kN/m, kN.

skipped.description: -- per kind, the rows RFEM listed for an object that is gone: a deleted object leaves an empty row carrying its number. Counted so that an import can say «97 node rows, 91 nodes» rather than quietly reading six fewer.

metadata.description: What the engineer wrote in the objects' comments, gathered -- the convention of calc/rfem_import/metadata_parser.py. Each object's own values stay on the object in `model`; this is the summary a reader looks at first.

keys.description: -- how many objects carry each key of the convention. Every count zero is a model nobody has annotated, which is the state every model starts in.

references.description: -- per key that names something existing elsewhere («position», «load»), the value against the objects that name it.

structures.description: The structures this import worked out: a connected component of the node graph, named by an @model comment where one names it, and merged with another component carrying the same name. ⚠️ A structure names its members and does not carry them.

key.description: -- what the structure is listed under: its name, or «member-<n>» for one nobody named, which is its lowest element and so stable while that element exists.

name.description: -- what @model called it; null where nothing did, and then the report cannot address it.

statics_name.description: -- what @label called the static model this structure becomes.

positions.description: -- the Woodcore positions its elements name, against the objects that name them.

results.description: The Schnittgrössen, where this import read them; the key is **absent** where it did not, so that «no results were read» and «this model has no forces» are not one thing. ⚠️ The distribution and nothing else: RFEM's own «Extrêmes» rows repeat a value the distribution carries, and the reader recomputes the same answer from it, so keeping them would be keeping a number twice.

kind.description: -- RFEM's own localised abbreviation for the kind of loading: CO, CC, SP, LF, DS.

members.description: -- the member number as a string against its stations, in order along it.

left_out.description: -- what the reader classified and did not keep, counted: the accounting that says the table was understood rather than partly skipped.

problems.description: Every note the import gathered, as it printed them -- so that a reader of this file knows what the import already knew. English, like every message of the pipeline; Woodcore's window says them in its own language from their codes (docs/typst/language.md §4bis).

values.description: What one object's comment held, by key of the convention: position, load, model, label, descr, be, note. A length is in metres.

restraint.description: A support or a hinge. ⚠️ The two read the same number the opposite way round -- «inf» holds a support and withholds a release on a hinge -- which is why `role` is kept beside `kind`.

kind.description: -- fixed, pinned, roller, spring, free for a support; moment, shear, normal, rotational-spring, rigid for a hinge: the words a Woodcore static model uses.

nodes.description: -- an RFEM support is one definition applied to a set of nodes, and that set may span two structures.

x.description: -- kN/m, or the string «inf» for rigid: JSON has no infinity.
